note: Research snapshot of pending Australian AML/CTF developments affecting legal practices. Every item is a watch item, not an obligation. Confirm each against its primary source at use time.

watch_items.item: Ministerial guidelines on legal professional privilege claims under section 242A
watch_items.status_at_snapshot: AUSTRAC's LPP guidance (last updated 1 July 2026) states the Minister for Home Affairs will issue guidelines covering review and challenge of LPP claims, further-information requests, handling of privileged information in searches and dispute resolution; not released at snapshot
watch_items.expected_trigger: Making of the final guidelines by the Minister as a notifiable instrument under section 242A
watch_items.status_at_review: Draft consulted, final not located. The Department of Home Affairs published Draft Legal Professional Privilege Guidelines 2026 (a first targeted round closed 1 August 2025; public consultation on the current draft closed 24 June 2026), and AUSTRAC reports Home Affairs and AUSTRAC are working to finalise them. On 2 Nov 2026 a Federal Register of Legislation name search for 'legal professional privilege' returned no instrument. The Home Affairs page could not be loaded and its search snippet still describes a draft
watch_items.review_basis: Federal Register search on 2026-11-02 (absence of a result is not proof none was made); Home Affairs page unreachable to automated access, so confirm it in a browser

watch_items.item: Further AUSTRAC guidance and worked examples for professional designated services
watch_items.status_at_snapshot: AUSTRAC states its reform guidance pages are updated regularly; the professional designated-services guidance and legal profession program starter kit continue to be expanded with examples and sector detail
watch_items.expected_trigger: Updates to the professional designated-services guidance, the legal profession program starter kit or new sector-specific releases
watch_items.status_at_review: Reported after the snapshot: the legal profession program starter kit moved from v1.0 (January 2026) to v1.1 (June 2026), which among other changes extended the conveyancing initial-CDD delay window and added a first-independent-evaluation section; AUSTRAC's updates page (checked 24 Sep 2026) shows v1.1 of 10 June 2026 as the latest release; its 20 August 2026 change only added the superseded v1.0 files with tracked changes. AUSTRAC also appears to publish legal-profession guidance under a newer reforms path. Verify the current starter-kit version and the guidance last-updated dates at use
watch_items.review_basis: Secondary sources and official pages seen in search results only; confirm against the primary source before relying on it

watch_items.item: Amendments to the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Rules 2025 and transitional rules
watch_items.status_at_snapshot: The AML/CTF Rules 2025 (F2025L01026) commenced 31 March 2026 (latest compilation F2026C00274). The AML/CTF Transitional Rules 2026 (F2026L00393) set staged deadlines: compliance-officer notification for newly regulated entities by the later of 14 days after enrolment or 29 July 2026; first independent evaluation of the program by 30 June 2029 to 31 December 2030 depending on the last two digits of the AUSTRAC account number; IFTI-to-IVTS reporting transition on 31 March 2029. Further amendment instruments are expected as the reform settles
watch_items.expected_trigger: Registration of amendment or transitional instruments on the Federal Register of Legislation
watch_items.status_at_review: The 29 July 2026 fixed date for compliance-officer notification by newly regulated entities has passed; for entities enrolling later, only the 14-days-after-enrolment limb now operates. No amendment instrument or compilation of the AML/CTF Rules 2025 later than F2026C00274 was located at review, but the official register could not be reached: recheck the latest compilation and any new amendment or transitional instruments at use
watch_items.review_basis: Official pages seen in search results only; confirm against the primary source before relying on it

watch_items.item: First annual compliance report cycle for tranche 2 reporting entities
watch_items.status_at_snapshot: AUSTRAC's obligations summary describes an annual compliance report about how obligations were met the previous calendar year; the first cycle covering tranche 2 entities' 2026 obligations, and its lodgement window, had not been the subject of dedicated tranche 2 guidance located at snapshot
watch_items.expected_trigger: AUSTRAC Online opening of the first financial-year compliance-report window, or any AUSTRAC notice changing the reporting period
watch_items.status_at_review: Reported after the snapshot: AUSTRAC's annual compliance reports page states that compliance reporting is moving from calendar years to financial years, with the next reporting period 1 July 2026 to 30 June 2027 and reports due within 3 months of the period ending (a 1 July to 30 September submission window). On that basis (an inference; the page does not address tranche 2 specifically) the first tranche 2 report would cover 1 July 2026 to 30 June 2027 and fall due by 30 September 2027. The snapshot's calendar-year description is superseded
watch_items.review_basis: AUSTRAC annual compliance reports page read on 24 Sep 2026

watch_items.item: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Amendment Bill 2026
watch_items.status_at_snapshot: Not on the register at the 14 August 2026 snapshot
watch_items.expected_trigger: Passage by both Houses, Royal Assent and commencement, followed by any AUSTRAC guidance on the changed LPP-form process
watch_items.status_at_review: Bill, not law: status 'Before Senate'. Introduced 12 Mar 2026; House third reading 16 Sep 2026 with 25 Government amendments; Senate first reading and second reading moved 12 Oct 2026; no Royal Assent. (Act No. 86, 2026, shown in the 1 Oct 2026 AML/CTF Act compilation, is a different Act.) The revised explanatory memorandum keeps the LPP change, requiring LPP forms to go to the agency that issued the notice ('the recipient must give the issuer', items 16 and 22). The supplementary explanatory memorandum describes the House amendments as moving the high-risk mechanism power to the Minister, adding consultation statements and commencing Schedule 1 on 1 July 2027; it does not describe any change to the LPP items. Also amends the 'financing of terrorism' definition, KYC requirements and politically exposed person definitions
watch_items.review_basis: APH bill page and the revised and supplementary explanatory memoranda read on 2026-11-02; the amendment sheet and third-reading text were not read, so confirm the LPP items against the passed text
